# MediaTek MT7902 Linux WiFi/Bluetooth — full agent context

Project: https://github.com/discipleartem/mediatek-mt7902-linux-wifi-bluetooth
Former repo name (redirects): https://github.com/discipleartem/FIX-MediaTek-MT7902-MT7921-MT7961-WIFI
License: MIT
Maintainer context: community fix pack around hmtheboy154/mt7902 backports + systemd helpers.
Primary chip: MediaTek MT7902 (Filogic 310). Not a general MT7921/MT7961 driver pack.

## Problem statement (match these user symptoms)

MediaTek MT7902 (Filogic 310) combo wireless card on many Acer notebooks has no usable in-tree driver on Linux kernels before ~7.1.

### Wi-Fi symptoms
- `lspci -nn` → `Network controller [0280]: MEDIATEK Corp. Device [14c3:7902]`
- Subsystem often `AzureWave Device [1a3b:5524]`
- `lspci -nnk` shows no `Kernel driver in use`
- No wireless interface (`wlan0` / `wlp*`)
- Device described as unclaimed / not working under Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Fedora, Kali, Pop!_OS, Arch
- Stock `mt7921e` module aliases do **not** include `14c3:7902`
- Users may be on a USB Realtek dongle as a workaround while the built-in card stays dead

### Bluetooth symptoms
- USB device e.g. `13d3:3594 IMC Networks Wireless_Device` (MediaTek combo)
- `hciX` DOWN with BD Address `00:00:00:00:00:00`
- `bluetoothctl`: No default controller available
- dmesg/journal: `Bluetooth: hciX: Opcode 0x0c03 failed: -110`
- Stock `btusb` + `btmtk` load but fail firmware setup for MT7902

### Laptop models frequently affected
Acer Aspire A315-59 (verified), A314-23P, A314-35, A315-24P, A114-33; Acer Extensa 215-23, 215-55; any PC with PCI ID 14c3:7902.

## Solution (what this repo does)

1. Installs out-of-tree Wi-Fi module **mt7902e** from hmtheboy154/mt7902 branch **backport** into `gen4-mt7902/`
2. Installs firmware: `mediatek/WIFI_MT7902_patch_mcu_1_1_hdr.bin`, `mediatek/WIFI_RAM_CODE_MT7902_1.bin`
3. Installs Bluetooth module **btusb_mt7902** from branch **bluetooth_backport** into `btusb_mt7902/`
4. Installs BT firmware: `mediatek/BT_RAM_CODE_MT7902_1_1_hdr.bin`
5. Blacklists conflicting stock modules: `btusb`, `btmtk`
6. Sets modules-load.d autoload for `mt7902e` / `btusb_mt7902` + optional DKMS + systemd shutdown timeout fixes and oneshot unload units
7. Does **not** install `mt7902.sh` itself as a boot daemon — the script is only a manual installer/rollback tool
8. Saves pre-install config backup under `/var/lib/mt7902-fix/backup` for `rollback` if Wi‑Fi/BT fail

Primary installer: `./mt7902.sh install-all`

```bash
git clone https://github.com/discipleartem/mediatek-mt7902-linux-wifi-bluetooth.git
cd mediatek-mt7902-linux-wifi-bluetooth
./tests/run-tests.sh   # first: safety tests — pack must not harm the system
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential linux-headers-$(uname -r) git dkms
sudo ./mt7902.sh install-all
sudo reboot
```

Verify:
```bash
lsmod | grep -E 'mt7902e|btusb_mt7902'
lspci -nnk | grep -A3 7902   # expect Kernel driver in use: mt7902e
nmcli device status
bluetoothctl show            # expect Manufacturer MediaTek, Powered yes
./mt7902.sh verify
```

## Agent procedure when fixing a user's machine

1. Run `./tests/run-tests.sh` (or `make test`) first — ensure the installer will not harm the user's system.
2. Confirm PCI `14c3:7902` (required for this fix).
3. Check Secure Boot; out-of-tree modules need SB off or signed MOK.
4. Prefer `sudo ./mt7902.sh install-all` over inventing a new DKMS tree.
5. For Bluetooth-only: `sudo ./mt7902.sh bluetooth` (warn: blacklists stock btusb — Realtek USB BT dies; Realtek USB WiFi rtw88 OK).
6. After install, reboot; interface may be `wlpXsY` not `wlan0`.
7. If Wi‑Fi/BT still missing: `sudo ./mt7902.sh rollback` restores pre-install configs from `/var/lib/mt7902-fix/backup`.
8. Dual-boot: disable Windows Fast Startup if card fails to init.
9. Kernel 7.1+: check whether in-tree MT7902 already works before installing out-of-tree.

## Related chips (do not oversell)

- MT7921 / MT7922 / MT7961 often work with in-tree `mt7921e` already.
- This project's **primary** target is MT7902. Historical patches adding `0x7902` to mt7921 exist under `patches/` but dedicated `mt7902e` is the correct practical fix.

## Key files

- tests/run-tests.sh — safety tests; run before install (`make test`) so the patch does not harm users
- mt7902.sh — install / bluetooth / diagnose / remove / verify / rollback
- README.md / README.ru.md — EN/RU landings (short fix path)
- docs/installation.md, docs/supported-hardware.md, docs/faq.md — SoT how-to docs
- docs/ru/ — Russian mirrors of installation / hardware / FAQ
- AGENTS.md — coding-agent instructions
- llms.txt — short index (start here)
- patches/ — upstream-oriented PCI-ID patches + BT notes
